title: One, four and five
summary: Three major chords make a useful family.

steps.title: One, four and five
steps.body:
In G major, I–IV–V–I is G–C–D–G. The three middle letters in these chord names do not change the rule: root scale degrees 1, 4 and 5 make major triads.

**Why it matters:** This is a common way to leave the tonic and return to it.

steps.title: See it on the fretboard
steps.body: Read each chord number before you play it. G is I, C is IV and D is V. All their notes belong to G major.

steps.title: Explore the sounds
steps.body: Try the same numbers in C major: C, F, G, C. Use the F barre shape only when comfortable; other correct note positions count too.
